CONCERNS OF REFERRAL SOURCE:
Primary Care Physician, Karen Vance, MD, dated 7/19/13: speech and language, social skills, sensory issues, cognitive delay (problem solving), and aggression. Medical history is remarkable for alleged intrauterine exposure to methamphetamine. Developmental history is remarkable for exposure to trauma.

CONCERNS OF PARENTS:
Behavior: Slow to react with directions/commands, sensory issues (e.g. sensitive to loud noises or temperature changes), toe walking, and meltdowns 2-5 times per week (screaming, hitting hair/bed, inconsolable).She is quiet, less engaging in group activities, focused for initial part then unengaged and fidgety. Safety is a concern as she has poor awareness of danger, she will climb/ jumps excessively and will wander away in public
Development: delays in speech and languages and suspected delays in overall cognitive development
-Developmental milestones: history of early milestones is not available
Gross motor: she was walking at 19 months of age, she can now walk, run and climb stairs, she is often klutzy and will fall easily, she is very active
Fine motor: Right handed, good pencil grip uses utensils like spoon and fork with much
spillage, she can drink from an open cup with spillage, she can take off all clothes and will try to dress herself.
Speech and language: at 3 years she had only 1 word, now she has more than a 100 words in
English and will combine 2�3 words. She uses words to get needs met about 50 % of the time, the rest she will whine or cry. She can follow single step commands. Emma Rose Callahan attends the Sunshine Bilingual Chinese/ English preschool but care providers there are mainly Chinese speaking and so are the children. Emma Rose Callahan does not speak any Chinese.
Social interactions and Play: she does not seek out peers for play and prefers to parallel vs. joint play, others have to initiate play for her to join them, and �he enjoys pretending with her dolls. No atypical play was reported. She does not seem to seek out physical aff_ection often, but will go to her Mother for help and sometimes to tell her she loves her.
Self care: she wants to be very independent and likes to learn to do things for herself
Feeding: No history of difficulties with chewing, swallowing, choking, gagging or vomiting. She has a good appetite.
Sensory: sensitive to noise, she will cling to Mother if she hears loud noises eg: public toilet flushes,
she does not like her hair brushed but also does not like it touching her face, she does not like shampoos, baths , she tolerates tags and clothing textures and she often toe walks
Elimination: No history of chronic constipation or diarrhea. She has regular Bowel Movements; she is toilet trained but needs reminders to go to the bathroom. She is starting to let parents know that she has to use the bathroom more often now. She is dry most nights.
